window: Monday, whenever you can before the DTS224 paper at 3pm, and again after it
goal: Logic and sets, which is the whole of test 1. Four lessons and you can answer fifteen of the forty-five questions the examiner has already set on this course.
drill: All 15 test 1 questions sit inside these lessons. Answer every one and read the verdict on the options you did not choose.

window: Monday evening, after the DTS224 paper
goal: Sets and functions. Functions alone are thirteen of test 2's thirty questions, and four of them turn on one sentence: domain in, codomain allowed out, range actually out.
drill: The function questions inside those lessons. If you can say the domain sentence without pausing, you have the largest single block on the paper.

goal: Proof, induction and sequences: another sixteen of test 2's questions. All three are vocabulary plus one method each, so they read fast on a fresh head.
drill: Lemma before, corollary after, theorem proved, conjecture not yet. Base case then step. Add for arithmetic, multiply for geometric.

window: Tuesday, 8:00 am to 9:30 am, then leave for the hall
goal: The three counting modules the tests never touched but the manual carries, then the cram sheet. Finish on the solved papers rather than on new material. Finish on the recipes, so the procedures are the freshest thing in your head.
drill: Nothing new. The past papers are no longer the target, since this paper is generated from the manual, so spend any time left on the cram sheet and the two objective tests instead.

window: Tuesday, only if you finish early and have time to spare
goal: The two solved past papers. They are NO LONGER the target, since this paper is generated from the course manual rather than from previous papers, and they ask about graphs, trees and Boolean algebra which the manual does not cover. Read them only as extra practice on the topics that DO overlap.
drill: Skip anything on graphs, trees, Boolean algebra, posets or lattices. None of it is in the manual.
